vision: HiveMind is an AI SRE crew that lives on your real telemetry: the moment Dynatrace Davis raises a real Problem on your service, HiveMind wakes up (no polling, no seed), diagnoses the root cause from real Grail data using Davis CoPilot, opens the exact GitLab fix as a reviewable MR, waits for one human approval, and then proves the service actually recovered against a Dynatrace SLO — the Site Reliability Guardian flips Fail to Pass, live, in the war-room. Any business connects its Dynatrace + GitLab in a 2-minute onboarding and watches a first real incident resolve end to end. The unfakeable proof is in the artifacts: a real problemId deep-linked into your tenant, a real DQL query, a real MR URL, and a Dynatrace-confirmed recovery — none of which a script can forge.

dynatrace_integrations.name: Davis Problem -> AutomationEngine Workflow webhook (kills the seed)
dynatrace_integrations.dynatrace_capability: Problems API v2 + AutomationEngine Workflow with a Problem trigger + HTTP Request action
dynatrace_integrations.how_hivemind_uses_it: Configure a real Workflow in the trial tenant: Problem trigger filtered to the demo service tag (app:checkout) -> HTTP Request action POSTs {{ event() }} to our existing /api/incoming/dynatrace. We must (a) widen the webhook parser in app.py from the flat DynatraceProblem model to accept the real event() shape (event.id, display_id, event.name, affected_entity_ids, event.status), and (b) expose the local backend via a cloudflared/ngrok tunnel and add that host to the Workflows global allow-list. seed_scenario.py is deleted from the live path. Demo line: 'We do not poll — the moment Davis raises a problem, Dynatrace calls us.'
dynatrace_integrations.wow_factor: The trigger is Dynatrace's own causal AI on real telemetry, not our script. Judges see a genuine Davis problemId arrive unprompted.

dynatrace_integrations.name: Davis CoPilot-driven diagnosis (NL -> DQL -> evidence -> NL)
dynatrace_integrations.dynatrace_capability: generate_dql_from_natural_language, verify_dql, execute_dql on Grail (spans+logs), chat_with_davis_copilot, list/execute_davis_analyzer
dynatrace_integrations.how_hivemind_uses_it: Detective already drives these via the Dynatrace MCP (agents/detective.py, stdio, Platform token, .apps URL). Two changes: (1) add list_problems + get_problem_details to its tool_filter so it pulls the REAL problem (rootCauseEntity + evidenceDetails) instead of re-deriving it; (2) flip its instruction from 'query fetch logs only, spans/metrics not populated here' to 'fetch spans for the rootCauseEntity and summarize p95 by 1-min bins' once OTLP spans are real. The Detective's intelligence becomes provably Dynatrace-native.
dynatrace_integrations.wow_factor: The investigation runs on Dynatrace's AI grounded in the customer's real telemetry, not our LLM guessing. The raw DQL string is surfaced in the UI as an unfakeable artifact.

dynatrace_integrations.name: Site Reliability Guardian recovery proof (Fail -> Pass)
dynatrace_integrations.dynatrace_capability: Site Reliability Guardian objectives (DQL indicators, severity 1=Fail..3=Pass) triggered via Workflow SRG action / POST /platform/automation/v1/workflows/{id}/run
dynatrace_integrations.how_hivemind_uses_it: Define one guardian for the demo service: objectives error-rate < threshold and p95 < 300ms as DQL indicators. Add a NEW orchestrator node 'recovery' AFTER the human approves + MR merges + the app redeploys: it triggers the guardian and reads back the verdict, emitting it as a war-room event. Before fix the guardian Fails(1); after the config revert it Passes(3). This is the single strongest 'real not scripted' beat.
dynatrace_integrations.wow_factor: We do not CLAIM the fix worked — Dynatrace's SRG validates the SLO recovered, quantified, live, against a threshold the judge can see.

dynatrace_integrations.name: Real telemetry ingestion via OpenTelemetry OTLP
dynatrace_integrations.dynatrace_capability: OTLP ingest endpoint (.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/otlp, http/protobuf, classic dt0c01 token, scopes openTelemetryTrace.ingest+metrics.ingest+logs.ingest) + Service Detection v2 from spans
dynatrace_integrations.how_hivemind_uses_it: Run a tiny checkout-service + payment-service in docker-compose, instrumented with the OTel SDK, exporting through an OTel Collector to jyl55158.live.dynatrace.com. Dynatrace auto-detects the services and dependency from spans alone (no OneAgent, no privileged Docker). This is what makes Grail data REAL. Belt-and-suspenders to make Davis fire fast: set a service fixed-threshold anomaly (no 7-day baseline wait) AND a metric event (violatingSamples 1/1) on a checkout.latency metric.
dynatrace_integrations.wow_factor: No OneAgent, no synthetic ingest — real request spans create a real Dynatrace service the moment traffic flows, and the regression shows up as a real latency curve.

dynatrace_integrations.name: Post-incident Notebook + Smartscape blast-radius + Davis forecast
dynatrace_integrations.how_hivemind_uses_it: Detective already best-effort writes a Notebook — make its content the full real investigation (the DQL it ran, the evidence, the root cause, the MR link, the SRG verdict) so an auditable record lands inside the customer's own tenant. Use Smartscape relationships from rootCauseEntity to render the war-room impact panel (which downstream services the regression touches). Optionally run GenericForecastAnalyzer on the error-rate metric to project return-to-baseline alongside SRG.
dynatrace_integrations.wow_factor: The audit trail and blast radius live INSIDE the customer's Dynatrace, reinforcing 'HiveMind lives in Dynatrace' rather than being a separate tool.

real_loop_architecture:
THE REAL LOOP (replaces scripts/seed_scenario.py end to end):

COMPONENTS (all local, docker-compose):
1. apps/checkout-service (Node+Express or FastAPI) -> calls apps/payment-service -> returns 200. Both auto-instrumented with the OTel SDK. payment-service reads a config knob `downstream_delay_ms` from a file that mirrors the GitLab repo file CodeArch edits (e.g. payment-service/config.yaml). Normal value 0.
2. apps/otel-collector (OTel Collector Contrib) -> OTLP/HTTP exporter to https://jyl55158.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/otlp with header Authorization=Api-Token <dt0c01>, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf.
3. apps/loadgen (20-line loop or k6) hitting /checkout at ~10 rps so Davis has a clean signal and stays above the low-load exclusion.
4. Existing FastAPI backend (app.py) + Redis + Phoenix from docker-compose.yml; add Postgres (auth + token store) and Next.js web.

INSTRUMENTATION + DAVIS CONFIG (one-time, in the tenant): tag the service app:checkout; set a service-level fixed-threshold response-time-degradation/failure-rate anomaly (builtin:anomaly-detection.services) AND a metric event (builtin:anomaly-detection.metric-events, staticThreshold ABOVE, violatingSamples:1 samples:1 for a ~1-min fire) on checkout latency. Both produce REAL Davis problems, readable via Problems API v2.

THE REGRESSION (real, deterministic, reversible): a commit/redeploy flips payment-service/config.yaml downstream_delay_ms: 0 -> 1200. /checkout p95 jumps ~80ms -> ~1.3s in real spans -> the fixed-threshold service slowdown AND the metric event both fire -> Davis opens a real Problem.

DAVIS -> HIVEMIND: a real AutomationEngine Workflow (Problem trigger, filtered to app:checkout) does HTTP Request -> POST {{ event() }} to /api/incoming/dynatrace (tunnel host allow-listed). REQUIRED CODE CHANGE: widen app.py's DynatraceProblem parser + _verify_dt_signature path to accept the real event() field names (event.id/display_id/event.name/affected_entity_ids/event.status); keep the HMAC fallback for local tests.

HIVEMIND DIAGNOSIS -> FIX: app.py spawns _run_incident_bg -> orchestrator/graph.py OrchestratorRunner.run. Detective (agents/detective.py) calls get_problem_details (ADD to tool_filter) for rootCauseEntity+evidenceDetails, then generate_dql_from_natural_language -> verify_dql -> execute_dql on real spans (UPDATE its instruction away from 'logs only'), concludes payment-service downstream_delay_ms regressed. CodeArch opens a real GitLab MR on the acme-commerce repo setting downstream_delay_ms back to 0 (existing repo_tree + GITLAB_PROJECT_ID path). LangGraph interrupt() pauses at the approval gate.

HUMAN -> RECOVERY: war-room approval card -> POST /api/incident/{id}/resume -> merge MR -> redeploy (compose restart / config reload of payment-service). ADD a new orchestrator node 'recovery' after Reviewer-approve: it triggers the SRG guardian (Workflow run API) and polls Problems API v2 until the Davis problem CLOSES, then emits a war-room event with the guardian verdict (Fail->Pass) + real before/after metric. Detective writes the post-incident Notebook with the real artifacts.

HOW TO RUN: `docker compose up` (redis, phoenix, postgres, api, web, checkout-service, payment-service, otel-collector, loadgen). Confirm the service appears in Dynatrace; run `scripts/inject_regression.sh` (flips the config + redeploys payment-service) to fire a real incident; watch the war-room channel pulse from the real webhook, the agents stream, approve, and the SRG tile go green. No seed_scenario.py in the path.
product_layer:
AUTH: Add Better Auth + Postgres (Docker), NOT Auth.js (Auth.js is in maintenance mode and forces JWT-only sessions for credentials, which is wrong for a tool holding customer Dynatrace/GitLab tokens). Better Auth stores users/sessions in our Postgres as opaque tokens -> instant server-side revocation; scrypt hashing by default. Concrete: lib/auth.ts with betterAuth({ database: pgPool, emailAndPassword: { enabled:true, minPasswordLength:8, autoSignIn:true, requireEmailVerification:false }, trustedOrigins:['http://localhost:3000'], plugins:[nextCookies()] }); route app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts via toNextJsHandler(auth); client createAuthClient() from better-auth/react. Next.js 16 gotcha: middleware.ts is renamed proxy.ts with a proxy export — use it for a coarse redirect to /sign-in, do real authz in the page/layout via auth.api.getSession({ headers }). The same Postgres holds each tenant's encrypted {dynatrace_url, dt_platform_token, dt_api_token, gitlab_url, gitlab_pat, project_id} -> multi-tenant, GCP-deployable (Cloud SQL).

LANDING (new app/(marketing)/page.tsx; move the war-room under app/(app)/ behind auth): copy the convergent incident.io/Rootly/Cleric structure in order — (1) Hero: headline 'From Dynatrace alert to merged fix — automatically.' subhead 'HiveMind watches your Dynatrace telemetry, finds the root cause in real production data, opens the GitLab fix, and watches your service recover — with a human approving every change.' dual CTA 'Connect your stack' / 'Watch a live incident'. (2) Metric bar (no logos yet): '6 specialist agents · Real Dynatrace Grail data · Human-approved fixes'. (3) 3 value props Detect -> Fix -> Recover. (4) The 6-agent workflow visualized (Detective -> ... -> CodeArch -> SRG) with the real problem flowing through — our differentiator surface. (5) 'AI that shows its work' (real DQL + problemId + MR URL). (6) Integration band: Dynatrace + GitLab + Gemini. (7) Trust band, lift the exact phrasing that maps to what we actually have: 'Never auto-remediates without human sign-off' (our LangGraph interrupt() gate) and 'Your data is never used to train models' (Vertex, not the consumer key). (8) FAQ ~8 Qs. (9) Closing CTA.

ONBOARDING (app/(app)/onboarding, 3-step wizard, progress rail): Step 1 Connect Dynatrace (tenant URL + Platform dt0s16 + classic dt0c01, with an inline 'How to get this token' disclosure naming each token's job). Step 2 Connect GitLab (URL + PAT with exact minimal scopes api+read/write_repository + 'revoke after demo'). Step 3 Run your first incident. The conversion lever is a per-integration 'Test connection' button (mirror Datadog's Test Authorization): on click hit Dynatrace whoami/trivial DQL and GitLab GET /user, show green 'Connected as <name> · <N> projects'. UI copy 'Tokens are encrypted at rest and never shown again'; store encrypted in Postgres; submit via Server Action over HTTPS, never NEXT_PUBLIC_/localStorage. End step 3 by triggering one real run and dropping the user into the war-room — the payoff is a real Dynatrace problem appearing, not a 'Setup complete' screen (mom test).

ui_system.icon_library: lucide-react (already installed; shadcn default, ~1500 icons, runtime strokeWidth for weight hierarchy). Keep @phosphor-icons/react (also already installed) ONLY for the marketing/landing hero illustrations, never in product chrome. Forbid Heroicons (reads AI-generated).
ui_system.palette: One dominant neutral (Vercel Geist gray) + ONE accent + four functional status colors used only for state. Dark-first, never #000: bg-base ~#0A0A0A, surface-2 ~#18181b (cards), surface-3 ~#1e1e22 (popovers). Depth from luminance + hairline borders white@8% (oklch(1 0 0 / 0.08)), NOT shadows. Text #EDEDED not pure white. Accent-brand desaturated in dark (oklch(0.66 0.15 250)). Status: success oklch(0.72 0.17 150)=recovered/merged, warning oklch(0.80 0.16 85)=degraded, destructive oklch(0.58 0.22 27)=incident, info oklch(0.66 0.15 250)=in-progress. The current globals.css already has the neutral oklch ramp and border white/10% — tighten border to /8%, add the four status + accent-brand vars to :root/.dark and @theme inline.
ui_system.typography: Geist Sans (UI) + Geist Mono (all machine strings: DQL, problemId, MR URLs, run IDs, timestamps, log lines) — already wired in layout.tsx via next/font. Scale 12/13/14/16/18/24/32. Chat body 14/1.5 weight 400 secondary @0.60; agent+channel labels 13/500 -0.01em; brief title 18-20/600; section headings 24-32/600 -0.02em. Mono on machine-generated strings is the instant 'engineering tool' signal.

build_order: Iter 1 (real telemetry): add apps/checkout-service + apps/payment-service (OTel SDK) + apps/otel-collector + apps/loadgen to docker-compose.yml; export OTLP to jyl55158.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/otlp (classic dt0c01, http/protobuf). Confirm the service + traces appear in the tenant. payment-service reads downstream_delay_ms from config.

Iter 2 (real Davis problem on demand): in the tenant set the service fixed-threshold anomaly + a metric event (1/1) on checkout latency; write scripts/inject_regression.sh that flips downstream_delay_ms 0->1200 and redeploys; verify a real Davis problem opens in ~1-3 min. Add list_problems+get_problem_details to detective's tool_filter and flip its instruction from logs-only to spans.

Iter 3 (close the real loop): create the AutomationEngine Workflow (Problem trigger -> HTTP Request -> {{ event() }} -> /api/incoming/dynatrace via cloudflared tunnel, host allow-listed); widen app.py's webhook parser to the real event() shape; confirm the war-room channel pulses from the real webhook, agents stream, CodeArch opens a real MR, approval gate works. Delete seed_scenario.py from the live path.

Iter 4 (recovery proof): define the SRG guardian; add a 'recovery' node to orchestrator/graph.py after Reviewer-approve that triggers the guardian + polls Problems API v2 until the problem closes, emitting the verdict; merge MR -> redeploy -> watch SRG flip Fail->Pass live; Detective writes the post-incident Notebook with real artifacts.

Iter 5 (product layer): add Postgres to compose; Better Auth (email/password) + proxy.ts redirect; move war-room under app/(app)/ behind auth; build the landing page (convergent 10-section structure) and the 3-step onboarding wizard with per-integration Test-connection; encrypt + store tenant tokens in Postgres.

Iter 6 (UI overhaul): swap emoji agent avatars -> Lucide icon+tone map; add the four status + accent-brand CSS vars; tighten borders to white/8%; kill gradients in brief-card/channel-sidebar/approval-card and shadow-lg in approval-card; surface real artifacts (problemId deep-link, DQL block in Geist Mono, MR URL, SRG verdict tile) in the brief + reasoning rows; run the grep-and-delete anti-slop pass.
risks: Davis CoPilot REST path/version isn't in public docs — drive nl2dql/chat strictly through the MCP tools (already how detective.py works), never hand-roll the HTTP call.

Davis auto-baselining needs ~1 week; do NOT rely on it for a live demo — use fixed-threshold service anomaly + a metric event (1/1) which evaluate immediately. Verify the trial tenant accepts samples:1 in the Settings UI and that builtin:anomaly-detection.services is exposed (set in UI first, then read the object to script).

OTLP host is .live.dynatrace.com (NOT .apps, which 404s) with classic dt0c01 + http/protobuf only (no gRPC/JSON). The MCP/Platform plane stays on .apps with the dt0s16 Platform token — don't cross the two auth schemes.
Workflows global allow-list blocks the webhook target until the tunnel host is added; the local backend must be reachable via cloudflared/ngrok for the real Workflow to call it.

Gemini is per-minute throttled on Vertex and the consumer-API-key pool is DEPLETED — keep ALL agent LLM calls on Vertex (genai.Client(vertexai=True)); the 6-agent chain plus a recovery poll can hit the per-minute cap, so keep cooldown/backoff and consider trimming the fan-out for the live run.

Real redeploy-to-recovery has latency (metric-event dealerting + SRG window) — the demo needs a believable ~2-4 min wait or a tightened dealertingSamples; rehearse the timing so the SRG Fail->Pass lands on camera.

Moving the war-room behind auth + into app/(app)/ touches existing routes/components mid-stream; do the auth/landing refactor in its own iteration after the real loop is green so it doesn't destabilize the working incident path.

Adding a 'recovery' node to a 709-line orchestrator graph with a Redis checkpointer risks serialization/resume regressions — keep recovery as a leaf node after Reviewer-approve, store its output as a plain dict like the other nodes.
